newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds close weaker, yield curve steepe.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds close weaker, yield curve steepe.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed weaker in light trade on Friday, with the yield curve steepening, amid the continued impact of yesterday's Bank of Canada monetary policy report, analysts said.

"The front end stability is still a bit of a follow through from yesterday's monetary policy report," said Mark Chandler, senior economist with Goldman Sachs Canada. "The longer end is weaking off a bit because of the poor performance of the U.S."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.30 to C$115.65 to yield 6.727 percent.
The U.S. 30-year benchmark fell 16/32 to yield 6.46 percent. The spread between the benchmark bonds narrowed to 27 basis points from 29 basis points at the close of trading on Thursday.
The Bank of Canada noted in its semi-annual monetary policy report on Thursday that there was a danger that the inflation rate would fall below the Bank of Canada's 1.0-3.0 percent target range.
"I don't think anybody is looking for an imminent move but the tone of the whole report was generally quite bullish," said Chandler.
In other prices, the Government of Canada's 7.0 percent of 2006 traded unchanged to yield 6.129 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond fell 8/32 to yield 6.18 percent.
The negative spread between the bond widened to five basis points from three basis points on Thursday.
Canada's three-month cash bill traded at 2.92 percent against the U.S. bill at 5.14 percent.
